decks.notes: The deck focuses on quickly assembling the Doomsday combo to win the game. It combines powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time with disruptive cards like Thoughtseize and Force of Will to protect the combo. The key is to set up a pile of cards with Doomsday that will allow the player to win the game on their next turn, usually with Thassa's Oracle. The deck also includes various tutors and fast mana like Black Lotus to help assemble the combo as quickly as possible while interacting with the opponent's game plan.

The crucial aspect of this Dimir Control deck is its ability to disrupt and control the opponent's game plan using a combination of counterspells, removal spells, and disruptive permanents like Null Rod. By denying resources and disrupting the opponent's strategy, the deck aims to outlast and outmaneuver its opponent, ultimately gaining control of the game and securing victory. With powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Time Walk, and Force of Will, this deck is well-equipped to handle a variety of threats and dominate the game through careful decision-making and strategic play.

The deck revolves around utilizing cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder to quickly fill the graveyard with key cards like Golgari Grave-Troll and Stinkweed Imp. It then uses the Dredge mechanic to continually mill cards from the library and get powerful creatures like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam onto the battlefield. The deck also includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Force of Negation to protect its combo pieces. Overall, the deck focuses on quickly overwhelming opponents with a relentless stream of graveyard-based threats.

The deck focuses on using a combination of efficient removal spells, countermagic, and card advantage cards to control the game and out-value the opponent. It also utilizes the powerful graveyard recursion ability of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion, allowing for additional value over the course of a game. By utilizing cards like Ancestral Recall, Force of Will, and Snapcaster Mage, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while establishing its own threats and advantage. The deck excels in long, grindy games where it can outlast the opponent and win through incremental advantage.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 Aggro-MUD deck focuses on utilizing artifact creatures and disruptive artifacts to control the game and overwhelm opponents with powerful threats. The deck aims to disrupt opponents' strategies with cards like Chalice of the Void and Sphere of Resistance while generating mana advantage through Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb. The inclusion of powerful artifacts like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge allows for additional utility and card advantage. Overall, this deck seeks to quickly establish board control and pressure opponents with a combination of disruptive elements and efficient threats.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategies while applying pressure with efficient threats like Oko, Thief of Crowns and Collector Ouphe. It aims to control the game through counter spells like Force of Will and Force of Negation, while leveraging powerful draw engines such as Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. By utilizing versatile cards like Abrupt Decay and Assassin's Trophy, the deck can handle a variety of threats. Through a combination of disruption, card advantage, and proactive threats, this BUG Midrange deck seeks to outmaneuver opponents and secure victory through a strong tempo advantage.

The deck focuses on utilizing graveyard recursion and card advantage to disrupt opponents and overwhelm them with a fast and powerful combo. Bazaar of Baghdad is a key card for digging through the deck and filling the graveyard with powerful creatures like Golgari Grave-Troll and Narcomoeba. Using cards like Creeping Chill and Prized Amalgam for additional damage and board presence, the deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces while maintaining control with Force of Will and Mindbreak Trap. With a strong mix of disruption and synergy, the deck can quickly overwhelm opponents and secure victory.

This deck focuses on disrupting your opponent's game plan with hatebears while applying pressure and beating down with aggressive creatures. The key strategy is to control the board with cards like Archon of Emeria and Anointed Peacekeeper, while using powerful hate cards like Chancellor of the Annex and Chalice of the Void to disrupt your opponent's plans. By combining disruptive elements with aggressive creatures, this deck aims to quickly overwhelm opponents and close out the game before they can recover.

The main focus of this Vintage 1 vs 1 Combo - Dredge deck is to quickly fill up the graveyard with cards like Narcomoeba, Ichorid, and Golgari Grave-Troll in order to return creatures from the graveyard to the battlefield and overwhelm the opponent with a large number of creatures. The deck also utilizes cards like Creeping Chill and Noxious Revival for additional damage and disruption, while including control elements like Force of Will, Mindbreak Trap, and Force of Negation to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's strategy. The deck's key strength lies in its ability to quickly assemble its combo pieces and overwhelm the opponent before they can respond effectively.

The main focus of this deck is to aggressively disrupt the opponent's strategies while developing a board presence. By playing hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, the deck seeks to slow down the opponent's spells and prevent them from executing their game plan smoothly. The addition of efficient mana sources like Ancient Tomb and Moxen allows the deck to deploy threats quickly and efficiently. By combining disruptive elements with a fast clock, this Aggro-Hatebear deck aims to control the game and overpower the opponent.

The deck focuses on quickly deploying threats that are difficult to deal with for the opponent, while disrupting their game plan with artifacts like Null Rod and Sphere of Resistance. With powerful mana acceleration from Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with big threats like Stonecoil Serpent and Golos, Tireless Pilgrim. The inclusion of Crucible of Worlds and Wasteland allows for consistent mana denial, giving the deck an edge in resource management. Overall, the deck aims to apply pressure early and control the game through efficient disruption and powerful threats.

The main focus of this deck is on control elements and card advantage. It utilizes powerful control spells like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares to disrupt the opponent's game plan while also using card draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to maintain a card advantage. The inclusion of an aggressive companion like Lurrus of the Dream-Den adds a unique twist to the control strategy, allowing for additional value from the graveyard. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Null Rod and Wasteland to further disrupt the opponent's resources and strategy.

This deck aims to win the game by using a combo involving Balustrade Spy, Undercity Informer, and Narcomoeba to mill the library and put Thassa's Oracle on the battlefield, causing the player to draw a card and win the game. It relies heavily on fast mana sources like Chrome Mox and Lotus Petal, as well as disruption spells like Force of Will and Pact of Negation to protect the combo. The deck has a low curve and high velocity, aiming to quickly assemble the combo pieces and win before the opponent can respond.

The deck focuses on using disruptive spells and efficient creatures to control the game, while also utilizing powerful draw and tutor effects to gain card advantage. It aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while developing its own board presence and card advantage through efficient plays. With a mix of countermagic, removal, and card draw, the deck aims to control the pace of the game and win through incremental advantages. The deck is built around a synergy between its spells and creatures to create a versatile and adaptable game plan.

The deck focuses on using Underworld Breach to cast multiple spells from the graveyard, generating infinite mana and drawing the entire deck with Brain Freeze. Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional recursion of low-cost spells. The deck is finely tuned with a mix of powerful Vintage restricted cards like Ancestral Recall and Time Walk, along with efficient mana sources like the Moxen. Force of Will and Force of Negation provide protection while disruptive cards like Flusterstorm and Pyroblast can help control the opponent's game plan.

This deck focuses on resource denial and disruption, utilizing powerful control spells like Force of Will, Force of Negation, and Wasteland to keep opponents in check. It also uses card advantage engines like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to maintain card advantage. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value by recurring cheap permanents. Overall, this deck aims to control the game through disruption, removal, and card advantage, ultimately outmaneuvering opponents to secure victory.
